attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: The firm part is an observation that recipe-from-photo code already existed. 'Code for Roose's app' slightly overstates 'code for it' (the idea), but the hedge 'presumably' on training is kept. Overall faithful.

contract.note: Requiring only a functional photo-to-recipe predecessor fits the speaker's own comparison (Deep-food, 'similar examples'). Leaving out the hedged training inference is correct. The plain reading is ordinary and fair.

evidence.note: Deep-food repository revision dated Oct 2020. Its README and deployment app describe fridge photo to ingredient recognition to recipe recommendation, with code. This predates March 2025.

A public issue dated May 2023 shows people trying to run the repository, which corroborates that it was public before Roose's essay. The credential/permission failure limits usability, not the existence of the code.

reviews.rationale: A dated public GitHub repository (Oct 2020) contains code that recognizes ingredients from a fridge photo and recommends recipes. A 2023 issue thread corroborates that it was public. This meets the support condition. Its usability problems (missing private credentials) do not contradict that the code existed. The hedged training claim is excluded.
